new_statements.quote: Betonung. Was die Betonung betrifft, so kann man es als stehende Regel betrachten, dass beinahe alle Wörter in ihrer nackten Form, d. h. wenn sie nicht in Verbindung mit anderen Wörtern gebraucht werden, den Ton auf der vorletzten Silbe haben. In der Rede erleidet der Accent jedoch mancherlei Verschiebungen, z. B.: kú-dsa kommen. ni-ma-kúdsa ich bin gekommen. ni-ku-dsá-ni ich bin am kommen. ka-dsá-ri? wann kam er? kámba er sagte. kambádsi? was oder wie hat er gesagt?
new_statements.translation: Stress. As regards stress, one may take it as a standing rule that almost all words in their bare form, i.e. when they are not used in combination with other words, have the accent on the penultimate syllable. In speech, however, the accent undergoes various shifts, e.g.: kú-dsa 'to come', ni-ma-kúdsa 'I have come', ni-ku-dsá-ni 'I am coming', ka-dsá-ri? 'when did he come?', kámba 'he said', kambádsi? 'what / how did he say?'

In der Rede erleidet der Accent jedoch mancherlei Verschiebungen, z. B.: kú-dsa kommen. ni-ma-kúdsa ich bin gekommen. ni-ku-dsá-ni ich bin am kommen. ka-dsá-ri? wann kam er? kámba er sagte. kambádsi? was oder wie hat er gesagt?' followed immediately by 'II. Das Dingwort.' -- ver…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In citation (isolation) forms the accent falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; when words combine with enclitics/suffixes (-ni, -ri, -dsi) the accent moves so as to stay penultimate in the enlarged word, and connected speech shows further shifts. Modern comparative work (Philippson 1991: 81, 415, 483, 496) adds that Pokomo also retains distinctive lexical H-tone ('accent') schemes on stems (BB/HB/BH), with penultimate prominence realised as length ('culmination de longueur, mais non de hauteur, sur la pénultième').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said by Würtz; none of the opened sources mentions secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Würtz: 'beinahe alle Wörter' (almost all words) — no list of exceptions given; accent 'shifts' in connected speech (examples all remain penultimate within word+enclitic). Philippson 1991: 42 characterises Pokomo as possibly having some words with no (tonal) accent and none with more than one; Nurse 2008 App.2 marks hú-na-guy-á 'we will buy' vs hu-na-gúy-a 'we buy'.
new_statements.domain_note: Würtz's rule is explicitly for the isolation/citation form of the word ('in ihrer nackten Form'); the domain of the penult count includes enclitic -ni/-ri/-dsi (ni-ku-dsá-ni, kambádsi). Philippson 1991: 496 says Pokomo prosody is a strict word-level system 'sans aucune influence du groupe prosodique' and (p.483) that the penultimate culmination is one of length, tone being separately distinctive.
new_statements.identity_note: lowe1441 is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for retired ISO 639-3 [poj] Lower Pokomo, merged into Pokomo [pkb] = poko1261 on 2008-01-14 (CR 2007-170: Upper/Lower Pokomo 'should be considered one language'). Glottolog's dialect nodes under poko1261 (Gwano, Kinakomba, Malalulu, Ndera, Ndura, Zubaki) are all Upper Pokomo; there is no Lower Pokomo dialect node, so a catalog entry belongs under poko1261 with a 'Lower Pokomo' dialect label. Würtz 1889 is specifically Lower Pokomo: he lived at Ngao on the lower Tana (1887-88), and the Rosetta Project files his sketch under poj. Philippson 1991 does not name the Pokomo variety he recorded. Ipu 1982 (held) is also Lower Kipfokomo; Shume 2017 is Upper Kipokomo.
